chunks: Al-ma'tam originally means the gathering of men and women in sorrow and joy. Then it became specifically used for the gathering of women for death, and it is said that it applies only to young women and no others (Al-Nihayah). It is also used for food prepared for the deceased (Fi).

key_terms.ٱلْمَأْتَمُ: a gathering, especially one associated with mourning

ai.seo_question: What does al-ma'tam mean in classical Arabic usage?
ai.summary: This entry explains the lexical meaning of al-ma'tam and how its usage became more specific over time. It first referred to a gathering of men and women in both grief and joy, then came to denote women's mourning gatherings, and also came to be used for food prepared for the deceased.
